tasks.objective: Give the MCP surface one definition of what a key name is, and construct the redactor's assignment rule from it, so that every name a tool is allowed to echo is a name the redactor would scrub the value of — by construction, not by comment. This is the half of finding f-envkit-mcp-surface/integration-97825fcf that lives below the tools: src/mcp/redact.ts's ENV_KEY ((?:export )?[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,127}=) refuses a leading digit and src/mcp/tools/*'s ECHOABLE_KEY (/^[A-Za-z0-9_]{1,128}$/) admits one, so the echo bound is NOT a subset of the redaction rule and the sentence in env-diff-keys.ts claiming the two modules agree is false. The repair direction is WIDEN, not narrow, and the reason is on the record: redact.ts's own docblock says 'Do not narrow the key pattern … either change reopens the hole this rule exists to close', over-redaction is its declared accepted failure direction, and narrowing ECHOABLE_KEY would make the comment true while leaving redactText blind to 9SECRET=hunter2 for every OTHER caller — redactError() is applied to arbitrary thrown messages, not only to .env documents. The hole is in the net, so the net is what widens. Scope is one new module, one existing module and their tests; neither tool file and not the manifest.
acceptance_criteria: src/mcp/keys.ts is new and holds the definition exactly once, as a character-class-and-bound fragment that both consumers derive from rather than two regexes that happen to look alike: a module-private KEY_BODY string (`[A-Za-z0-9_]{1,128}`), an exported anchored ECHOABLE_KEY built as new RegExp(`^${KEY_BODY}$`) for membership tests, and an exported ENV_KEY string fragment built as `(?:export )?${KEY_BODY}=` for embedding in an assignment pattern. Two literals that must stay identical is the shape that produced this epic; one literal that both forms are computed from is the shape that cannot drift.

src/mcp/redact.ts defines no key pattern of its own. Its local ENV_KEY constant is deleted and the name is imported from './keys.js'; ENV_ASSIGNMENT is otherwise unchanged, including the whitespace-then-assignment boundary lookahead, which continues to embed the same fragment on both sides. The docblock paragraph beginning 'Over-redaction is deliberate' keeps its 'Do not narrow the key pattern' sentence verbatim and gains one sentence recording that the pattern was WIDENED to admit a leading digit, that the definition now lives in ./keys.ts, and that the reason is the subset invariant AC[3] grades.

The behaviour change is asserted, with the null measured rather than assumed: redactText('9SECRET=hunter2') returns '9SECRET=[redacted]' and redactText('1_TOKEN=abc') returns '1_TOKEN=[redacted]'. Under the null — the shipped src/mcp/redact.ts at integration head 049765c, re-measured in-session against dist/mcp/redact.js, whose ENV_KEY line is byte-identical to the source — both calls return the input byte-identical: '9SECRET=hunter2' -> '9SECRET=hunter2' and '1_TOKEN=abc' -> '1_TOKEN=abc'. That is the finding, reproduced as a failing test before the fix exists.

The subset invariant is proven mechanically and never again stated in prose alone, because prose is precisely what failed here. A test iterates a fixed corpus of candidate key names — at minimum 'A', '_', 'A0', '_0', '9SECRET', '1_TOKEN', '0', a 128-character name and a 129-character name, all drawn from [A-Za-z0-9_] — and for every name k asserts: if ECHOABLE_KEY.test(k) is true then redactText(`${k}=hunter2`) !== `${k}=hunter2`. The implication is one-directional on purpose: the redactor is allowed to scrub more than the tools may echo (that is the accepted over-redaction), and is never allowed to scrub less. The 129-character name is in the corpus as the control — it is not echoable, so the implication is vacuous for it, and a test that passed only because the corpus was all-echoable would be indistinguishable from one that works.

Every existing behaviour of redact.ts survives the widening, asserted rather than argued. test/mcp/redact.test.ts is extended and never weakened: no test in it is deleted, skipped, renamed, or has an expected value changed. In particular the named residual in the docblock still holds and gains a test if it lacks one — redactText('NOTE=alpha FOO=beta') returns 'NOTE=[redacted] FOO=[redacted]', measured in-session at head 049765c, so the literal FOO still stands as if it were a key and every value run is still gone. If widening the pattern changes the expected value of an existing assertion, that is a finding and not an edit: record the failing test name and its actual/expected verbatim in the result's structured output and report error spec.spec-gap to the planner rather than adjusting the assertion.

ECHOABLE_KEY is exercised by this task even though its importers arrive in task-2-tools-share-key-bound, so it does not land as an unreferenced export nobody has run: test/mcp/keys.test.ts asserts the membership rule directly on the corpus above, and src/mcp/keys.ts's module docblock names src/mcp/tools/env-lint.ts and src/mcp/tools/env-diff-keys.ts as the importers task-2 attaches, with the finding id f-envkit-mcp-surface/integration-9b8279e9 as the reason.

functional_clauses: The invariant, stated once and graded by AC[3]: the set of names ECHOABLE_KEY admits is a SUBSET of the set of keys the redactor's assignment rule recognises. Anything a tool may echo as a name is something whose value redact scrubs. The reverse containment is not required and must not be added — the redactor scrubbing more than the tools echo is the accepted direction.

Widen the redactor; do not narrow the echo bound. Both edits would make the two rules agree, and only one closes anything. ECHOABLE_KEY's character class is not touched by this task and must be byte-identical after it: the tools' echo behaviour does not change, so no report a client already relies on changes shape.

This task moves the definition of a key and admits a leading digit; it does not touch SECRET_KEY, SECRET_SHAPED, MAX_DEPTH, redact()'s recursion, redactError(), or the boundary rule's structure. A change to what counts as a credential SHAPE is a different question with different evidence and belongs to a different task.

The widening has a cost and it is accepted, not hidden: a diagnostic line like `2=3` or `1024=x` is now redacted where it was not before. That is over-redaction on text the surface was never obliged to echo, and it is the direction redact.ts's docblock already commits to. Do not add a heuristic to tell a 'real' digit-leading key from an incidental one — nothing in the text distinguishes them and the guess would guess toward under-redaction, which is the failure this module exists to prevent.

tasks.objective: Close the two leak directions the closing spec review of v1 found in the redactor, give the echo bound the rationale v1 asserted but never assigned to a task, and replace three criteria that could not fail with assertions that can. Ground truth measured at e22cb5f by running node against the built dist: (a) redactText('PASSWORD=my secret 2024=phrase here') returns 'PASSWORD=[redacted] 2024=[redacted]', where '2024' is a fragment of the secret VALUE and was scrubbed at the epic base 049765c — this epic's widening of the key fragment shipped a new under-redaction, which task-1 functional_clauses[0] ('never allowed to scrub less') and [3] ('the cost is over-redaction') both forbid; (b) ECHOABLE_KEY.test('AKIA0123456789ABCDEF') is true and redactText('AKIA0123456789ABCDEF=hunter2') returns '[redacted]=hunter2' — the VALUE survives, so the epic's headline subset invariant is false for every echoable name that is itself credential-shaped, because SECRET_SHAPED rewrites the key first and the injected bracket breaks ENV_ASSIGNMENT's boundary anchor; (c) src/mcp/keys.ts carries no over-exclusion rationale anywhere, which task-2 functional_clauses[3] asserts it does. The shipped manifest descriptions are already true and are not edited here; what is missing is a test that pins them, because task-3 AC[7] delegated that grading to a command that never reads a description. Scope is the redactor, the key module, and four test files.
acceptance_criteria: The under-redaction regression is gone and pinned by exact-match assertion in test/mcp/redact.test.ts: redactText('PASSWORD=my secret 2024=phrase here') === 'PASSWORD=[redacted]'. The whole value run, including the embedded digit-initial token, is scrubbed. An assertion of the form not.toContain('2024') alone does not satisfy this criterion — the criterion this task exists to replace was weak in exactly that way, and the expected string is short enough to write out.

The pre-existing letter-initial residual is unchanged and is pinned as such in the same file: redactText('NOTE=alpha FOO=beta') === 'NOTE=[redacted] FOO=[redacted]'. It predates the epic base 049765c and is out of scope. A change that also closes it is a change to the boundary rule this task did not ask for; a change that widens it is a regression. The test comment states which of the two directions is accepted here and why, in one sentence.

The subset invariant is true and is graded on the VALUE, not on the key. test/mcp/redact.test.ts asserts, for every name k in a corpus, that ECHOABLE_KEY.test(k) implies redactText(`${k}=hunter2`) does not contain the substring 'hunter2'. The corpus contains, at minimum: 'A', '_', 'A0', '_0', '9SECRET', '1_TOKEN', '0', a 128-character name, 'AKIA0123456789ABCDEF' and 'ghp_ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP'. The last two are the point: v1's criterion compared the whole output to the whole input, which a key-only rewrite satisfies while the value leaks, and its corpus held no credential-shaped name, so it was vacuous on the only class that broke it.

The carve-out at test/mcp/redact.test.ts:252-265 ('known gap: a secret-shaped key breaks the invariant (pre-existing, not fixed here)') is deleted rather than edited, because the gap it names is closed by AC[2]. Deleting a test is otherwise a failed task under this epic's standing clause; this is the single named exception, and the result records it in one sentence naming this criterion.

src/mcp/keys.ts gains a comment paragraph stating the accepted failure direction of the echo bound and why it was chosen: a key name outside [A-Za-z0-9_]{1,128} is counted and never named, so a legitimate but unusual name (one containing a dot, or longer than the bound) is over-EXCLUDED from every listing rather than risked in an output. The paragraph is graded mechanically: `grep -ci 'over-exclu' src/mcp/keys.ts` returns at least 1, and the paragraph names the opposite direction it rejects (naming a key the redactor would not scrub) in the same breath. It does not claim over-redaction is the only failure direction of the redaction rule — AC[0] is the counter-example, and the false half of that sentence is why v1's version of it could not simply be restored.

test/mcp/key-bound.test.ts's set-equality case stops being degenerate. Its right-hand fixture is non-empty and shares at least one in-bound key with the left, so missingFromRight is a proper non-empty subset of the left listing and sharedCount is at least 1. The assertion states both expected sets by literal value. v1's version wrote an empty right side, where missingFromRight trivially equals the whole left listing and the interesting case — a name both files define, echoed by env_lint and correctly absent from missingFromRight — was never exercised.

test/mcp/surface.test.ts pins both tool descriptions against BOTH reasons a defined key goes unnamed, read through the manifest the server actually loads rather than through a CLI check that never inspects a description. For env_lint and env_diff_keys alike, the assertions require the description to state (i) the [A-Za-z0-9_] / 128-character bound and that anything outside it is counted and not named, and (ii) that an in-bound name which itself looks like a credential comes back as the redaction marker and still counts as in-bound. Regexes or exact substrings, never a snapshot. The shipped descriptions at e22cb5f already satisfy both; this criterion makes that non-regressible, which is what task-3 AC[7] was reaching for and could not do.

The two mis-qualified citations at test/mcp/redact.test.ts:203 and :228 read 'plan v5 AC[2]' and 'plan v5 AC[3]'; both are replaced by the fully-qualified form this repo uses elsewhere in the same file (compare src/mcp/redact.ts:46, 'AC[3] of envkit-mcp-followup/task-1-key-shape-module'). 'plan v5' in test/mcp/ denotes the PREVIOUS epic, envkit-mcp-surface — the same file cites 'plan v4 AC[3]' at :92 and 'plan v4 AC[6](b)' at :146 meaning exactly that — so the labels currently resolve to unrelated criteria.

The two bare citations in test/mcp/key-bound.test.ts ('AC[3](i-iii),[6]' and 'AC[6]') are qualified the same way. Bare AC[n] already means envkit-mcp-surface in this directory (test/mcp/env-lint.test.ts:71), so bare AC[3] currently names two unrelated criteria one directory apart. Scope is the citations this epic added; the citations that predate 049765c are not touched.

`git diff --stat 049765c..HEAD -- test/mcp/` shows env-lint.test.ts and env-diff-keys.test.ts still untouched by this epic, and the full suite passes at 299 tests or more with no test skipped, renamed away or weakened beyond the single deletion AC[3] authorises.

functional_clauses: The redactor is never allowed to scrub less than it did at the epic base 049765c. That is the clause this task exists to restore, and it is the one clause a fix here can violate while every existing test stays green — the suite at e22cb5f passes with the leak in place.

Do not narrow ECHOABLE_KEY or the outer key fragment. The echo bound stays [A-Za-z0-9_]{1,128}: narrowing it would restore the redactor's behaviour by shrinking the set of names a tool may echo, which trades a leak for silent under-reporting and undoes task-1 and task-2 in the same stroke.
Do not weaken SECRET_SHAPED, remove a pattern from it, or make any credential shape conditional. It is the net that catches tokens with no key to hang them on.

If the evaluation order of the two nets changes, the change is justified in the result against a worked counter-example, because order is load-bearing: SECRET_SHAPED currently runs first so that a bearer token containing '=' is caught whole, and an assignment pass running first would leave its prefix standing. A fix that reorders without pinning that case is incomplete.

The docblock in src/mcp/redact.ts is updated to match the behaviour that ships. Its paragraph beginning 'This residual cuts BOTH ways' currently documents the digit-initial leak as accepted; after this task that sentence is false and a false comment in the file whose whole job is truth-in-redaction is worse than none.
No handler, manifest, server or config file is edited. mcp.manifest.json is deliberately NOT claimed: its descriptions are already true at e22cb5f and this task adds the test that keeps them true.
Extend the four claimed test files; do not delete, skip, rename or weaken any test in them beyond the single deletion AC[3] names.
